forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

news_drafts.headline: Derby mid-year report: short-term borrowing between councils cost 3.8% to 5.5% over the period
news_drafts.lead:
Derby City Council's treasury management mid-year report, put to the Council meeting on 18 November 2026, says the cost of short-term borrowing from other local authorities rose throughout the period it covers. Rates ran between 3.8% and 5.5%. The report describes this as inter-authority lending, where councils lend spare cash to each other, usually for a few months.

The paper says the rise was driven by councils relying more on the short-term market. It adds that "low cash levels and the non-receipt of SEND grants are also likely to have contributed to a high borrowing demand". SEND stands for special educational needs and disabilities.

The report puts the average short-term loan market rate at 4.65% on 30 September 2026, against 5.2% twelve months earlier.
news_drafts.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Treasury Management Mid-Year Report

news_drafts.headline: Derby expects £20.947m grant that would cut its schools-funding deficit to about £11m by March 2027
news_drafts.lead:
Derby expects an indicative £20.947m High Needs Stability Grant from government, with payment currently expected on 30 November 2026. The grant follows approval of the city's Local SEND Reform Plan. SEND stands for special educational needs and disabilities, and high needs is the part of school funding that covers it. The council's quarter 2 monitoring report to Cabinet says the sum is 90% of the accumulated deficit on the dedicated schools grant (DSG), the government grant that funds schools, at the end of 2025/26. That deficit stood at £23.274m. The paper says the grant would reduce the cumulative DSG deficit from £32.729m at the end of 2026/27 to circa £11m. Derby remains responsible for the other 10% and for any future in-year pressure.

The in-year DSG deficit for 2026/27 is forecast at £9.455m, a favourable change of £0.518m from quarter 1. The budget set in February forecast £9.966m. The paper names the high needs block as the main driver, against an allocation of £69.248m. Placements with other local authorities' special and mainstream schools are forecast £0.880m over budget, and Further Education providers £1.792m over.

The council's Delivery Plan performance report for quarter 2 keeps the strategic risk on high needs budget balance as Threat 16, rated Red: Highly Probable, with Very High impact. It says the SEND Placement Sufficiency Strategy "is not yet in place". The same report records the action to establish a new high needs funding model as completed.

news_drafts.headline: Derby Cabinet papers put Waste Treatment Centre write-down at about £51.4m, with government permission sought
news_drafts.lead:
Derby City Council expects to write down the value of the Derby and Derbyshire Waste Treatment Centre by about £51.407m after deciding not to operate the facility, according to the Medium Term Financial Strategy paper before its Cabinet on 7 October 2026. The council's chief finance officer is required to ask government for a capitalisation direction (permission to treat day-to-day spending as if it were capital spending, so it can be paid for by borrowing or asset sales).

The paper describes the figure as an impairment and write-back, which is an accounting entry recording that the plant will no longer produce the benefits the council had expected from it. It says this is not a new cash cost. The paper puts the council's current estimate at "approximately £51.407m" and says the scale of the effect is why the direction is needed, to manage what it means for the council's day-to-day budget (revenue spending).

The paper is part of the council's medium-term financial strategy, its financial plan for the next few years. The material available to this desk does not give the timetable for the government's decision, nor how the council would cover the sum if permission were granted.
news_drafts.paper_title: Item 14 - Medium Term Financial Strategy including National Issues and Derby Focus

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Treasury Management Mid-Year Report
findings.headline: Cash available within one month was £93.6m at 30 September 2026, against a liquidity indicator target of more than £15m.
findings.detail: The council reports that it maintained adequate liquidity through Q2 2026/27 and that the liquidity indicator was met.
findings.matters: Liquidity headroom is the first test lenders and peers apply when judging whether a council can meet short-term obligations without new borrowing.
findings.figures: Cash available within one month £93.6m; target >£15m
findings.quote: The Council has maintained adequate liquidity throughout Qtr.2 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Treasury Management Mid-Year Report
findings.headline: Average return on the council's deposits and investment portfolio fell from 3.81% in 2025/26 to 3.50% at 30 September 2026.
findings.detail: Average investment size rose to £134.826m, while total interest earned on deposits in the period to 30 September 2026 was £2.057m. The paper reports the investment return against a benchmark of 3.00%.
findings.matters: Falling investment returns reduce treasury income, which finance directors compare across councils when assessing income pressures.
findings.figures: Average return 3.81% (2025/26) and 3.50% (30/09/2026); benchmark 3.00%; average portfolio size £134.826m; interest earned £2.057m to 30/09/2026
findings.quote: Average Return on deposits/ investment portfolio 3.81% 3.50%

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Treasury Management Mid-Year Report
findings.headline: The PWLB 10-year certainty rate rose from 5.62% at the start of the period to 6.17% at the end.
findings.detail: The paper also reports 20-year rates moving from 6.13% to 6.61% and 50-year rates from 6.01% to 6.37%. It says the council's strategy is to borrow in the short to medium term while monitoring longer-term rates.
findings.matters: Councils refinancing from the PWLB are working against the same rates, so the rise in long-term rates affects their own replacement funding decisions.
findings.figures: 10-year PWLB certainty rate 5.62% to 6.17%; 20-year 6.13% to 6.61%; 50-year 6.01% to 6.37%
findings.quote: The PWLB certainty rate for 10-year maturity loans was 5.62% at the beginning of the period and 6.17% at the end.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Treasury Management Mid-Year Report
findings.headline: The paper cites the non-receipt of SEND grants as a likely contributor to high short-term borrowing demand, with short-term local authority borrowing costs between 3.8% and 5.5% during the period.
findings.detail: The paper says the cost of short-term borrowing from other local authorities rose throughout the period, driven by councils relying more on the short-term market. It cites low cash levels and the non-receipt of SEND grants as factors likely contributing to high borrowing demand.
findings.matters: Non-receipt of SEND grant funding is a cash-flow pressure that finance directors elsewhere are also tracking, and short-term rates above Bank Rate affect the cost of managing that gap.
findings.figures: Short-term local authority borrowing cost 3.8% to 5.5%; average short-term loan market rate 4.65% at 30/09/2026 vs 5.2% 12 months earlier
findings.quote: Low cash levels and the non -receipt of SEND grants are also likely to have contributed to a high borrowing demand.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Treasury Management Mid-Year Report
findings.headline: The treasury management budget is forecast to be balanced as at 30 September 2026, with any variance to be met from the treasury management reserve.
findings.detail: Variances are to be managed within the treasury management reserve, which the paper says is set up to smooth fluctuations in the capital programme, borrowing and funding requirements.
findings.matters: Other councils managing treasury budgets under pressure will want to know how this council is absorbing variance and whether that smoothing reserve is being relied on.
findings.figures: None given for the variance; the paper reports a balanced forecast
findings.quote: As at 30 September, the budget is forecasting a balanced position.
